root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward tenderness, compassion, and beneficent favor.
root_idea.development: The semantic field develops from compassionate feeling to enacted beneficence, while the womb and kinship are connected through the origin and bonds of birth. The divine names الرَّحْمَٰن and الرَّحِيم express this field as encompassing and abundant mercy, respectively, though the sources also record some synonymy between them.

senses.definition: To show mercy, compassionate favor, or beneficent care toward someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of human or divine action. With God as subject, it denotes beneficent action rather than human emotional tenderness; Quranic forms include active, passive, and imperative constructions.

senses.definition: Womb: the bodily place and receptacle in which offspring originate and develop.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural أَرْحَام, used for wombs in contexts concerning gestation and birth.

senses.definition: Kinship, a family relationship, or ties of blood relationship.
senses.usage_conditions: In أولو الأرحام and related constructions, it denotes kin relations. Legal usage can include relations without a prescribed inheritance share or agnatic status, and ذُو رَحِمٍ مَحْرَمٍ denotes a relation whom it is unlawful to marry.
Used comparatively and in the superlative expression أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ, “the most merciful of those who show mercy.”

senses.definition: Compassion; merciful concern expressed toward another.
senses.usage_conditions: A noun of the mercy-and-compassion branch, used in the Quran in the construction بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ.

senses.definition: Mercy: compassionate favor or beneficent care.
senses.usage_conditions: The ordinary Quranic abstract noun; when attributed to God, it denotes enacted beneficence rather than a human emotional state. It may be possessed, bestowed, received, or sought.

senses.definition: A divinely bestowed prophetic commission or gift of prophecy.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-attested specialized interpretation of God’s تخصيص someone with His mercy; no modern verse location is assigned here because the relevant Lane citation uses historical citation conventions and the packet does not independently establish that exact location.

senses.definition: Sustenance or the means of subsistence.
senses.usage_conditions: A specialized Quranic use explicitly identified in the expression occurring in the passage cited as Quran 41:50 by the lexical evidence.

senses.definition: Rain as an act or manifestation of mercy.
senses.usage_conditions: A specialized Quranic interpretation of mercy in a rain-related context; the cited Lane reference is not converted into a modern verse location here.

senses.definition: Plenty, abundance of herbage, or the goods and comforts of life.
senses.usage_conditions: A specialized Quranic use in contexts of abundance; the cited Lane references are preserved as lexical evidence without reconstructing modern locations.

In وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْمًا, the form conveys an affectionate or compassionate relation; the Quranic interpretation should not be reduced to the ordinary abstract noun رَحْمَةٌ without noting this relational nuance.

senses.definition: Abounding in mercy; merciful and beneficently disposed.
senses.usage_conditions: Applied to God as a divine epithet and also to human beings, including the Prophet. With God as subject, the term denotes beneficent action rather than emotional tenderness; in the Quran it commonly occurs as a predicate or epithet.

senses.definition: The All-Merciful or universally merciful; the divine name expressing encompassing mercy.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quran as a name or epithet of God and not as an ordinary human adjective. The lexical discussion characterizes its mercy as encompassing all creation, including believer and unbeliever.

senses.definition: One who shows mercy; merciful persons.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural active participle رَاحِمِينَ, used in the superlative construction أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ and in descriptions of those who show mercy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pardon or forgive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical extension of showing mercy, kept separate from the Quranic sense of beneficent mercy because the supplied Quran-focused evidence does not independently establish pardon as a distinct Quranic use of this verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer a uterine complaint after giving birth, sometimes resulting in death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a woman or female animal, including a camel, ewe, or goat; the lexical descriptions concern a disorder of the womb after parturition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a water-skin, to become spoiled and unable to retain water after being neglected or insufficiently greased.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized inanimate use concerning a water-skin after it has been seasoned and then left untreated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Being connected by relationship or kinship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An infinitival noun denoting connection by family relationship; this is distinct from the Quranic nominal use of أَرْحَام for kin relations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To invoke mercy for someone, as in saying, “May God have mercy on you.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II construction with عَلَيْهِ; it is a conventional formula or expression of a wish for divine mercy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To express or seek pity and compassion, or to show mercy toward another; sometimes to do so intensely or deliberately.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V usage may express a wish that God show mercy, an expression of pity, or an affected effort to show compassion; the sources report variation in its grammatical and semantic analysis.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To show mercy, pity, or compassion to one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or demand mercy, pity, or compassion from someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form X transitive request for another person’s mercy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name of Mecca, understood as “source of mercy.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name expression rather than an ordinary productive meaning of رُحْمٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The coming forth of the womb as a result of disease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized obstetric term, distinct from the ordinary noun for the womb and from the condition described by رَحُومٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A felt relationship, consanguineous sympathy, or sense of blood connection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of the kinship noun, sometimes expressed in the phrase حَاسَّةُ رَحِمٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vulva.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical figurative or transferred use distinct from the primary sense “womb.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tenderness or compassionate feeling considered apart from its resulting beneficence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical distinction within the mercy field; the Quranic form-level sense is stated in terms of mercy and beneficent care, while this entry records the abstract feeling considered on its own.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pardon or forgiveness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical nominal extension of mercy, not separately claimed as a Quranic lexical sense here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The invocation “May God have mercy on you.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive expression derived from the Form II mercy-invocation construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pity or compassion, especially in the fixed paired expression contrasting pity with fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Primarily occurs coupled with رَهَبُوت or its corresponding form in the proverbial expression “fear is better for you than compassion.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Treated or regarded with mercy or favor, and defended or supported.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical adjectival use in which the adjective describes the recipient of merciful treatment rather than the agent who shows mercy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ewe or she-goat, having a swollen womb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-health adjective, distinct from the active-participle sense “showing mercy.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Treated or regarded with much mercy, pity, or compassion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The doubled consonant marks an intensive Form II passive-participial sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name of Medina.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name use of the passive-participial form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The object of mercy; in later usage, a deceased person regarded as having died in the true faith.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The later conventional honorific use is broader in reference but historically connected with being the recipient of divine mercy.

cautions: The distinction between رَحْمَٰن and رَحِيم is presented as a supported usage distinction, not an absolute etymological rule; the lexical evidence also records authorities who treat them as synonymous.

Several Lane Quran citations use historical citation conventions. Specialized interpretations have been represented where supported, but modern verse locations are given only where the QAC packet independently supplies the location securely.
